_source.note: Closed vocabularies read out of the code, not out of the README prose. A canvas showing a value that is not in one of these lists is a fabrication, and check.mjs refuses it.

scopeTypes.note: All four are readable behind the caller-scope gate. Write accepts two.

searchIndexReasons.note: THREE named reasons a document is not searchable, and they are not the same thing. A JSON record was never eligible. A scanned PDF has no text layer. A corrupt PDF failed extraction. Every file browser in the world collapses these into absence from the result set.

provenanceRequiredKeys.note: A missing or invalid key REFUSES the write with 400. It does not default.

revisionRule.verbatim: Uploading a SECOND time with the identical docSlug is a new VERSION of the SAME document (currentVersion increments, entityId is unchanged, response carries revision: true) rather than a counter-suffixed sibling document
revisionRule.note: This is what makes a submittal identity stable across revisions.

readGate.cite: README.md G-106 defect #3, src/identity.mjs parseServiceIdentities / identityAllowsAnyScope
readGate.verbatim: A read refuses with 403 -- anonymous or a token scoped to a different tenant alike -- unless the bearer token resolves to a SMART_FILES_SERVICE_TOKENS identity holding a grant for the resource actual (scopeType, scopeId).
readGate.defaultDeny: SMART_FILES_SERVICE_TOKEN is deliberately NOT auto-granted read access to every scope; an environment that has not configured SMART_FILES_SERVICE_TOKENS reads nothing, by design, rather than keeping the old defect as a silent default.

facts: requireReadScope runs BEFORE any data is touched, so the search gate is exactly as strict as every other read route.
Only the CURRENT version of a document is searched.
Results carry entityId, title, snippet and rank metadata only, never blob bytes.
search_text IS NULL, never the empty string, is the one honest not-indexed value.
The tsvector column is STORED and generated, not trigger maintained, so the index cannot drift out of sync with search_text.

placements.verbatim: Every uploadFileToFolder write used to hard-code a folder placement, even when the real target was already knowable -- e.g. smartcity-dashboards municode calendar scraper uploads a meeting documents with no way to say which meeting.
placements.note: targetType and targetId now travel together and are validated against the smart_file_placements CHECK constraint. Wiring the municode scraper to actually pass targetType meeting is a separate change in that repo and is NOT done.

shippedTable.note: The shipped table already carries three of the good properties: Version, Who can see it, and Referenced (placements). It carries NOTHING about searchability and NOTHING about provenance, and those are the two the product is strongest on.

shippedCopy.peopleView: Every grant, every link, every revoke, with a name and a time. This is the page a city attorney opens.
shippedCopy.accessRail: A share link is a row in this list with a name and a time, not a URL that exists off the record. Revoke sits at the same weight as the grant.
shippedCopy.emptyRoom: Files are private to the tenant that owns them. Nothing has been created here, and nothing has been shared with it.
shippedCopy.bringCaveat: This page is chrome against fixture data. It is not a live Drive sync.

mountedAt.verbatim: This view mounts the serving Smart Files host with its own product top bar suppressed. It does not copy the browser.
mountedAt.note: The dashboards Files surface is a MOUNT POINT, not a second implementation. Designing Files in dashboards would be designing a frame. The product is here.
